Step 3 (Risks in sports): Prick the edge of the blister with a needle that has been sterilized in a flame (p. 87).

Sports Core Field Standard Principle 2: Tobacco smoke interferes with proper lung growth and function (p. 10).
Sports Core Field Standard Principle 3: It coats the lungs with sticky tars and injures the airways and air sacs of the lungs (p. 10).
Sports Core Field Standard Principle 4: Athletes need their lungs working atpeak capacity (p. 10).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 (Sports Core Field Standard): Usingtobacco can leave you gasping for air when you need (p. 10).
Step 2 (Sports Core Field Standard): Being tobacco-free gives you the stamina to playsports (p. 10).
Step 3 (Sports Core Field Standard): The blood carries the poisons from smoking to all parts of the body, from thebrain to the bladder (p. 10).
Step 4 (Sports Core Field Standard): Scientists now know that smoking causescancers of the mouth, the larynx (voice box), the lungs, and thekidneys (p. 10).
